findings.title: Materials' 53-point lens gap defies its percentile
findings.body: Materials sits at the 40th percentile on forward earnings yet its trailing multiple is at the 93rd percentile, a 53-point split that is the widest in the table. Analysts are underwriting 124 percent earnings growth, which would be a historic reversal for a sector whose trailing earnings have already been bid up to near-five-year highs.

findings.title: Health Care's 86 percent growth is priced in
findings.body: Health Care's forward and trailing multiples are nearly identical in percentile terms, yet the forward lens implies 86 percent earnings growth. That compression of 46 percent between the two lenses means the market is fully paying for a margin expansion that would be extraordinary for a defensive sector.

findings.title: Communication Services' forward percentile collapses
findings.body: Communication Services trades at the 2nd percentile on forward earnings, down 18 points in a month, while its trailing multiple sits at the 27th percentile. The 25-point gap between lenses implies 54 percent growth, but the market is pricing in a deterioration so severe that the forward multiple has fallen to a five-year low.
